title: credit-aware-routing-and-fragmented-chunk-handshake-to-stabilize-toolcalls
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Gateway: introduce credit-aware routing to reduce proxy queueing on large toolcall streams; improve stream proxy resilience with fragmented-chunk handshake for fncall/tooling frames; no user-facing API changes, opt-in via route policy flag.
description: Motivation: We observed several incidents where long-running tool/function calls (especially those producing structured JSON arrays and large attachments) caused the gateway stream proxy to accumulate large in-flight buffers, which in turn increased tail latency and triggered compatibility fallbacks for OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: 1) credit-aware routing: a routing heuristic that factors in downstream proxy credit/backpressure and per-route buffer occupancy when selecting a target host/variant; 2) fragmented-chunk handshake: an explicit small handshake frame for fncall/structured-output flows that allows proxies to detect fragmented payloads and assemble them incrementally with bounded headroom before handing them to the compatibility layer. Summary of changes (commits): - commit 1: introduce credit tracker and routing policy hooks (gateway/router.go, routing/policy.md) - commit 2: implement fragmented-chunk handshake and reassembly in stream proxy (proxy/stream_proxy.go, proxy/handshake_test.go) - commit 3: extend OpenAI compatibility handler to honor incremental-assembly signals and avoid pessimistic framing (compat/openai/handler.go) - commit 4: add e2e regression tests and a small perf harness (tests/e2e/toolcall_fragmented.yaml, perf/tools/credit_routing_bench.go) - commit 5: docs and changelog updates (docs/gateway/route_policies.md, CHANGELOG.md) High-level changed areas/files: - gateway/router.go: new routing hook credit-aware route_score that penalizes targets with >X KB buffered fncall bytes - proxy/stream_proxy.go: introduce handshake frame type 0x7F (FRAG_HANDSHAKE); reassembly buffer limited to configurable headroom (default 64KB) - compat/openai/handler.go: read incremental-assembly flags and stream partial structured output to client while compatibility transformations run - tests/*: new deterministic tests reproducing the previous regression and asserting bounded buffer usage Small illustrative snippet: "if route.creditEstimatedBufferedBytes > route.maxBufferedKB*1024 { score -= 50 // deprioritize }" Review conversation (condensed into a single narrative): - Ravi: "Nice approach; two quick asks: make the default headroom conservative (64KB) and add telemetry for 'credit_rejections' so SRE can track how often routing avoids a host." - Maya: "Agreed on 64KB default; added metric gateway.routing.credit_rejections and exposed route.policy.headroom_kb to route config." - Elena: "Can the handshake be versioned? We need to avoid breaking older proxies in mixed clusters." - Maya: "Handshake frame includes a 1-byte version field; compatibility code ignores unknown versions and falls back to legacy chunking behavior." - Tom: "Saw a flaky test in proxy reassembly on first CI run. Did you root cause?" - Maya: "Yes — test assumed deterministic goroutine scheduling. Rewrote test to poll for condition and added a 50ms max-wait. Reran CI." CI and merge: - First CI run (linux-integration) failed on proxy/handshake_test.go due to timing flakiness; subsequent push fixed tests and all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, perf-smoke). - Metric checks and canary smoke were green in staging. - PR approved by Ravi and Elena; merged via squash. Operational notes and rollout: - This change is feature-flagged behind route.policy.enable_credit_aware_routing and route.policy.fragmented_handshake so we can rollout per-cluster. - Recommend enabling in staging for 48h and monitoring gateway.routing.credit_rejections, proxy.reassembly.headroom_allocs, and client.compatibility.fallback_rate. - If credit_rejections spike above 1% of routing decisions, consider increasing route.policy.headroom_kb or decreasing penalty weight. Rationale and impact: - Credit-aware routing reduces tail latency by preferring hosts with available headroom; it trades off slight routing imbalance for bounded buffer usage. - Fragmented-chunk handshake reduces worst-case proxy memory growth for very large structured outputs and stabilizes fncall handshakes for OpenAI-compatible streams. - No public client API changes; OpenAI compatibility layer behavior is relaxed to accept incremental assembly when handshake present. Related work and follow-ups: - Follow-up: add autoscaling signal based on aggregated buffered bytes across pool (ENG-6621). - Follow-up: expose per-route default headroom presets tuned for embeddings vs chat vs tooling (PM-121).
notes: This PR targets gateway surface behavior and OpenAI compat plumbing; kept change surface limited and feature-flagged to allow staged rollout. All narrative in description is a continuous string as required by repository artifact guidelines.
